**Finding submitted: IP — missing (fallback cure proposed).**

- **Investigation:** I read every section (Articles 1–10) and searched for ownership, "Content", and data terms. The Agreement never allocates IP: HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site (§§1.1–1.7) at its own cost, yet there is no ownership, assignment or licence provision for the Site, code or look-and-feel, and no statement of our rights in our Content, user information and customer/order data — which appear only as Confidential Information in §8.1. §5.2 (artistic/editorial control) and §1.4 (access to HDI's tools) fall short of any IP grant.
- **Target level:** Fallback. Because HDI bears all development cost (§§1.2, 1.6) and takes a revenue share (§3.1), demanding a full assignment of the Site is not the shortest complete cure; the licence-back fallback is.
- **Change:** One new §5.5 inserted after §5.4 — HDI retains its generic tools and know-how; we get a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and other deliverables for our business; and any HDI licence in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for us is limited to processing it solely to provide the services. All eight fallback elements are carried by that single operation, with no ancillary boilerplate added.
